limitations: Clinical guidance applies with trained professional judgment; a chat classifier is neither a validated risk assessment nor an emergency-response service.

title: Psychosis and schizophrenia in adults: prevention and management (CG178)
issuer: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
summary: NICE guidance addresses recognizing and caring for adults with psychosis or schizophrenia, emphasizing timely professional support and sustained recovery. Experiencing an unusual belief alone does not establish a diagnosis.
limitations: Published February 2014 and reviewed July 2025; addresses professional clinical practice in a UK health system. It does not provide an automated diagnostic rule or establish that spiritual explanations are clinical symptoms.
rights: Metadata and original short paraphrase only; subject to NICE rights notices.

title: Generalised anxiety disorder and panic disorder in adults: management (CG113)
issuer: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
summary: NICE guidance describes stepped healthcare management for adult generalized anxiety and panic disorders and options for education, self-help, psychological treatment and medical care.
limitations: Initially published 2011, with recommendations amended in 2020; scope is adults with anxiety/panic in clinical settings. No recommendation proves chatbot-delivered therapy is effective or permits medication advice.
rights: Bibliographic pointer and original summary; source content not copied.

title: Bipolar disorder: assessment and management (CG185)
issuer: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
summary: NICE guidance covers professional recognition, assessment and management of bipolar disorder across ages; later revisions include medication-specific safety updates.
limitations: Published 2014; specific recommendations updated September 2025. Clinical assessment requires qualified practitioners. Reduced sleep, intensity or grandiosity described to a chatbot must not automatically produce a bipolar diagnosis.

issuer: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
summary: SAMHSA describes trauma-informed principles including safety, transparency, peer support, collaboration, user choice and cultural/historical awareness. These are design principles, not proof of chatbot therapeutic efficacy.
limitations: Conceptual public-health/organizational framework, not randomized evaluation of AI support. The 2014 principles should be checked for later guidance and translated into testable behavior.

limitations: Applies to workplaces, policies and trained service systems; not a claim that reframing a worker's thoughts remedies structural employment pressures or unsafe conditions.

title: The efficacy of acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) for depression: A systematic review and meta-analysis
summary: A meta-analysis of ten randomized clinical trials investigated ACT for patients diagnosed with depression; the authors reported effects on depressive and anxiety symptoms and psychological flexibility, with varying certainty.
limitations: Only ten trials; the review rated certainty for depressive symptom effects low, anxiety moderate and flexibility high. Clinical ACT trials do not establish efficacy or safe delivery by TherapyBot, and subgroup comparisons need cautious interpretation.
